task: input.js/main.js/physics.js - yank on pointerdown with cooldown (impulse along rat->pivot plus tangential damping, never energy-adding), plus wrap and yank counters in telemetry
done_when: A scripted bumper-level run records wrapContacts > 0 and a yank measurably reduces the wrap; AND a yank-spamming batch shows no sustained-speed or hits-to-clear advantage over a no-yank batch at the same seeds
context: The riskiest step. A yank that adds energy becomes the dominant strategy and collapses the game into click-spam (L0076: every dense reward term is a new exploit surface), so the exploit check is a measurement rather than a judgement call. DONE 2026-09-07: yank on pointerdown, 0.6s cooldown, clamped so it can never raise speed. Verified at real swing speed (44-89 px/step): 0 of 6 yanks raised speed - the clamp binds every time, so a yank redirects velocity toward the pivot without changing its magnitude. Unwind confirmed: 5 of 5 yanks reduced rope bend, several dramatically (10.2->1.2, 16.9->0.06). Exploit A/B at identical seeds, spam 0.6s vs none: hits to clear identical on both L1 and L7, p50 speed within 2.5%, peak within 1 - no advantage. CAVEAT: ropeBend measures total turning along the rope, which conflates a genuine obstacle wrap with the rope crumpling when slack; L1 has no bumpers yet records the most contacts (92, all rope-vs-target).

task: Pick the hand-speed cap and sub-step count by feel, then make them defaults and retune damage for the new speed range
done_when: A hand cap and sub-step count are chosen from browser play, set as defaults, DAMAGE_SCALE retuned against a fresh human calibration, and the rope no longer visibly passes through obstacles at speed
context: User reported 2026-09-09 that the rope passes through obstacles when spinning fast. Root cause measured: updatePivot wrote the pointer position straight into the constraint, so the hand teleported up to 234px per frame (p90 107) and whipped the rat to 249px/step against 44px bumpers - Matter has no continuous collision detection, so more than half of all steps moved further than a bumper is wide. Sub-stepping alone cannot fix it (contacts never plateau: 48/39/100/157/266/288/843 at 1..24 sub-steps) and reducing gravity would not either, since the player drives the pivot directly. The hand cap bounds the system at its source: rat peak 249 -> 149 (hand 80) -> 101 (hand 40) -> 65 (hand 25). Implemented as dev-tunable with defaults unchanged so the user can choose by feel. CAVEAT: bot clear rates at low caps are unreliable - its pump policy was built for an uncapped hand and fails entirely at hand=25. UPDATE 2026-09-11: the user tested and the rope still tunnels. Measuring rope segment velocity directly (with sub-stepping, body.velocity IS per-sub-step displacement) shows why my hand=40 recommendation was wrong: I estimated rope displacement from the RAT peak, but rope segments whip far faster than the rat (432 vs 247 px/step). At hand=40/subs=4, 26.3% of rope samples still exceed the 44px bumper diameter; only hand=25 gets it to 1.4%, which is a large feel change. Sub-stepping does not help - 4 to 8 sub-steps made it slightly WORSE (26.3% to 30.5%), because better constraint solving stiffens the rope and it whips harder. A rope-segment speed clamp cuts over-44 samples to 3.5% but cannot bound displacement, because the constraint solver repositions bodies directly regardless of velocity (ropeMax stayed ~280 under a cap of 12). CONCLUSION: no parameter fixes this. Matter 0.19 has no continuous collision detection and this game sits squarely in the regime where discrete collision fails. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-12 by task 123/124: swept collision fixed the tunneling this task existed to mitigate, without capping the skill ceiling. The hand-cap, sub-step and segcap knobs remain available and documented as tuning levers, but choosing values for them is no longer needed work.

task: physics.js - manual continuous collision detection for rope segments via Matter.Query.ray: sweep each segment from its previous to its new position each sub-step, and on a hit against a target or bumper place it at the contact point and kill its normal velocity
done_when: Rope segments no longer pass through targets or bumpers at any achievable speed, with the rat speed and hand behaviour left untouched, and the gate still green
context: The correct fix for the tunneling the user reported. Matter 0.19 ships no CCD, but Matter.Query.ray is present and verified working against a bumper in this build. The rope is the only body that needs sweeping - the rat is large enough and carries the damage - so this stays contained and changes no gameplay feel, unlike the hand cap (task 122) which caps the skill ceiling and still leaves 26% of samples tunneling. DONE 2026-09-11: sweeping implemented in step() after each Engine.update, defaulting ON. Measured at the settings the user actually plays (hand uncapped, 1 sub-step): segments found INSIDE an obstacle fell from 2.19% to 0.00% on L7 and 2.58% to 0.20% on L4, while rope contacts rose 36->173 and 91->360 - the rope now registers what it was silently missing. Hits to clear unchanged (5->5, 6->5), clear rate 100% both, and physics cost 0.174 -> 0.166 ms/frame, i.e. no measurable cost, because segments that moved less than their own radius are skipped. The residual 0.20% on L4 is the point test ignoring segment radius: a segment whose centre is outside can still overlap by up to 3.5px.
